classification_reason: Acceptance criteria describe required behavior (suppress near-duplicate alerts, configurable window, differentiate by severity/active state) but leave several implementation-shape decisions open: how the controller signals 200-vs-201, where the config lives and how it's bound, where the duplicate lookup is implemented, and the header-name constant location. Resolved via conservative, repo-consistent decisions below; see requirement-analysis.md.
story_description: As an operator, I want near-duplicate alerts suppressed so I'm not flooded with repeats of the same issue.
acceptance_criteria: On POST /api/alerts, if an active alert with the same Title (case-insensitive) and the same Severity was created within the last 15 minutes, do not create a new row; return 200 OK with the existing alert and response header X-Duplicate-Suppressed: true
A genuinely new alert still returns 201 Created
The suppression window in minutes must be configurable via appsettings.json and not hardcoded
Do not suppress across different severities or when the prior matching alert is inactive
exact_source_files: AlertService.Data.SQL/Repositories/AlertRepository.cs (implement FindActiveDuplicateAsync: case-insensitive title, IsActive==true, Severity match, CreatedDate >= cutoff)
AlertService.API/Controllers/AlertsController.cs (branch CreatedAtRoute vs Ok + X-Duplicate-Suppressed header based on CreateAlertStatus)
exact_source_files_note: Exceeds the default 5-file cap deliberately: the story requires a new config/options concept, a repository-level query addition, a result-type change to the service contract, and a controller branch, touching every layer per repo-profile.md layering (Common -> Data -> Data.SQL -> API options/service/controller). This is the smallest file set that satisfies all four acceptance criteria.

design_decisions.result_pattern: Add CreateAlertStatus { Created, DuplicateSuppressed } enum and CreateAlertResult(CreateAlertStatus Status, AlertResponse Alert) record in IAlertService.cs, mirroring the existing AddAlertTagsResult/AddAlertTagsStatus pattern. IAlertService.CreateAsync returns CreateAlertResult instead of a bare AlertResponse; the controller branches on Status.
design_decisions.config_binding: Introduce AlertService.API/Options/AlertSuppressionOptions.cs with a single int DuplicateWindowMinutes property (default 15). Bind via the standard ASP.NET Core IOptions<T> pattern: builder.Services.Configure<AlertSuppressionOptions>(builder.Configuration.GetSection("AlertSuppression")) in Program.cs, injected into AlertManagementService as IOptions<AlertSuppressionOptions>. Chosen over raw IConfiguration access (the one existing precedent in Program.cs for Database:ApplyMigrationsOnStartup) because AlertManagementService needs a testable, injectable value and service-architecture.instructions.md favors correct DI configuration; appsettings.json gains a new top-level AlertSuppression:DuplicateWindowMinutes section (value 15).
design_decisions.duplicate_lookup: Add a dedicated narrow repository method IAlertRepository.FindActiveDuplicateAsync(string title, Severity severity, DateTime createdAfter, CancellationToken) implemented in AlertRepository using the existing case-insensitive .ToLower() comparison pattern plus a.IsActive && a.Severity == severity && a.CreatedDate >= createdAfter, ordered by CreatedDate descending, first match. Chosen over reusing GetAllAsync's broader filter set for clarity, testability, and to express the exact AC #1/#4 predicate in one place rather than composing it at the call site.
design_decisions.header_constant: Add AlertConstants.DuplicateSuppressedHeaderName = "X-Duplicate-Suppressed" instead of a hardcoded string literal in the controller, consistent with AlertConstants.cs being the repo's convention for small shared constants.
design_decisions.time_math: At POST time, cutoff = _timeProvider.GetUtcNow().UtcDateTime - TimeSpan.FromMinutes(options.Value.DuplicateWindowMinutes); duplicate query filters CreatedDate >= cutoff. Window value comes only from configuration, never hardcoded in the service or repository.
design_decisions.response_status_mapping: Controller: CreateAlertStatus.Created -> CreatedAtRoute(nameof(GetById), new { id = result.Alert.Id }, result.Alert) (201); CreateAlertStatus.DuplicateSuppressed -> Response.Headers[AlertConstants.DuplicateSuppressedHeaderName] = "true"; return Ok(result.Alert) (200).

out_of_scope: Suppression across endpoints other than POST /api/alerts (no retroactive suppression of existing rows)
Configurable suppression scope beyond Title+Severity (e.g. matching on Description)
Any change to GET/PUT/DELETE alert endpoints
Auditing/logging of suppressed duplicates beyond the existing logger usage already in AlertManagementService
missing_facts: TO_BE_DISCOVERED: whether DuplicateWindowMinutes should have a documented default in appsettings.json (recommend 15, matching AC #1's literal example) versus requiring explicit configuration with no fallback. Resolved conservatively as a configured default of 15 in appsettings.json; confirm during /implement-story if the repo's config conventions require otherwise.

TO_BE_DISCOVERED: whether a duplicate match should consider only the single most recent matching alert or whether ties/multiple matches are possible. Resolved: the repository query returns the first/most recent active match within the window; multiple historical active matches are not expected given suppression prevents them from being created in the first place.
